key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: GRADUAL onset over days to weeks, often chronic with seasonal flares. LOCATION: SEBORRHEIC areas - scalp, face (eyebrows, nose, ears), chest, back. DURATION: Chronic condition with acute flares lasting days to weeks. CHARACTER: ERYTHEMATOUS (red), SCALY, OILY patches. AGGRAVATING: STRESS, weather changes, certain shampoos/soaps. RELIEVING: ANTIFUNGAL shampoos, topical steroids, avoiding triggers. TIMING: Chronic with seasonal flares, worse in winter. SEVERITY: 2-4/10 itching, mild to moderate. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: MILD ITCHING (pruritus), scaling, may have secondary bacterial infection from scratching. KEY POSITIVES: Erythematous patches, scaling, seborrheic distribution, oily appearance. KEY NEGATIVES: No fever, no systemic symptoms, no vesicles or bullae.

red_flags: Rash with fever and systemic symptoms - possible secondary infection, needs urgent evaluation
Rash with pus or increasing pain - secondary bacterial infection, needs urgent evaluation
Rash involving >30% of body surface - severe flare, needs urgent evaluation
Rash with signs of secondary infection - fever, pus, increasing pain - needs urgent evaluation
Rash with difficulty sleeping due to severe itching - severe flare, needs urgent evaluation
